market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: Despite a temporary ceasefire, a permanent peace deal requires overcoming decades‑long hostility, nuclear and sanctions disputes, and proxy wars, all in under three months. Even with engagement, the shift from a short‑term truce to a lasting settlement is historically unprecedented and extremely unlikely.
evidence_points: A temporary ceasefire on April 7, 2026, does not signal willingness to permanently end military hostilities; similar past ceasefires collapsed.
Permanent peace would demand resolution of core issues (nuclear program, sanctions, regional influence) that remain far apart.
No US president has normalized relations with Iran; the current maximum‑pressure stance and deep bureaucratic inertia weigh heavily against a rapid deal.
sources_consulted: Hypothetical resolution criteria describing the April 7, 2026 ceasefire
Historical precedent of US‑Iran diplomatic failures (JCPOA collapse, maximum‑pressure campaigns)
Expert commentary on the structural obstacles to a durable US‑Iran peace
